audit.title: Digital Transfer Agent (DTA) Technical Standard

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong opening: "The Chainlink Digital Transfer Agent (DTA) technical standard defines how transfer agents and fund administrators can expand their operations onchain…" is self-contained and quotable. The "Next steps" section is thin but acceptable.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H1→H2, 0 level skips, 10 bullets aid extraction. Weak point: a single long body section under the H1 with no sub-headings phrased as questions; no summary table.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weakest dimension. Measured: 0 numerals, 0 units, vague quantifiers "most, quickly." No named chains, no product counts, no launch date, no throughput figures.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 8 links but 0 to primary sources; mostly chain.link marketing pages plus one Swift press release. No links to the actual technical standard spec or regulatory frameworks it claims to support.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The bolded lead sentence is a good verbatim-liftable definition. "Digital Transfer Agent" itself isn't defined as a term for readers unfamiliar with transfer agency.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified from served HTML — CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read, but measured facts confirm absence.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code; acceptable for an overview page, scored neutral. Not the right lever here.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Answers "what is DTA" implicitly but has no "How do I…", no troubleshooting, no definition of who needs it. Full lifecycle lives on other pages.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Consistent naming ("Chainlink DTA technical standard" throughout) aids entity resolution; marred by fluff ("easiest and most reliable path").

audit.summary: This is a short conceptual overview (362 words) introducing the Chainlink DTA technical standard and routing to a "How It Works" page. Its biggest GEO strength is a crisp, liftable opening definition and consistent product naming; its biggest opportunity is the near-total absence of concrete specifics (0 numerals, 0 supported-network names, vague quantifiers "most," "quickly") plus missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates). As an entry-point page it reads more like marketing than reference — it will be skimmed and paraphrased rather than cited authoritatively unless it anchors claims in numbers and primary sources.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to replace vague quantifiers
recommendations.where: Body bullets under the lead paragraph.
recommendations.issue: "quickly and easily offer the following services," "reducing the need for manual reconciliation" — 0 numerals on page.
recommendations.change: Name the supported blockchains explicitly, state the number of live chains, the initial go-live date ("Now live in production" → give the date/quarter), and any settlement latency or NAV update cadence. Replace "most" with the actual figure.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims (chains, dates, limits) are among the highest-lift changes for citation; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/entity-phrased H2 defining the term
recommendations.where: Immediately after the lead, before the services list.
recommendations.issue: No heading matches "What is a Digital Transfer Agent?" — the exact question a dev/agent types.
recommendations.change: Add `## What is a Digital Transfer Agent (DTA)?` with a one-sentence definition of transfer-agent function onchain, then `## What does the Chainlink DTA standard support?` over the bullet list.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the answer is in body text.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema + canonical + last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about: "Digital Transfer Agent"`, and a self-referencing canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust for agents.

recommendations.title: Cite primary sources, not only marketing pages
recommendations.where: "facilitating adherence to applicable regulatory frameworks" and the CCIP/ACE/NAVLink list.
recommendations.issue: 0 links to primary sources; regulatory-framework claim is unlinked.
recommendations.change: Link the DTA technical standard spec/whitepaper and name+link the specific regulatory frameworks referenced; keep the existing product links.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative references raise credibility and citation rate; unsupported compliance claims are unliftable.

recommendations.title: Trim marketing fluff
recommendations.issue: "provide the easiest and most reliable path for market participants."
recommendations.change: Replace with a factual capability statement (what it runs on, what it produces).
recommendations.why: Engines reward clean factual prose; superlatives without evidence are not quoted.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "most," "quickly," "easiest and most reliable path" — unquantified.
Marketing fluff in the lead paragraphs ("capture the emerging opportunity").
Stale/undated: no visible last-updated or publish date despite "Now live in production" claim.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is indexed there.
Metadata absence should be confirmed against raw `<head>` (not captured in this run); the CLI should pass it for a definitive read.
Third-party/earned citations (e.g., the Swift pilot) are off-page authority signals worth leveraging but not editable here.
